title: The love feast
hook: a simple shared meal of bread and water with testimonies

segments.voice: Yesterday, the covenant prayer: a promise made again, with nothing held back. Your line was no longer my own. Where did your uncounted hour go? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-nine.

In Corinth, the church's shared meal has gone wrong. Some arrive early and eat their own suppers before the others get there. Paul doesn't soften it: "one is hungry, and another is drunken." A meal meant to make them one family was splitting them into rich and poor. And still the early church kept eating together. Jude's short letter mentions their "feasts of charity," in the King James words. Charity there is love. Love feasts. Methodists, Moravians, Brethren and others still keep a meal by that name. Today's word: the love feast.

Acts describes the first believers "breaking bread from house to house," and says they "did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart." Meat there just means food. A table where everybody eats. John Wesley learned the love feast from the Moravians and brought it into Methodism, and he kept it plain on purpose. Simple bread or cake, and water, passed from hand to hand, with a shared cup. No fine food, nothing to show off. Corinth's problem would be hard to repeat at a table like that. Then came the real meal: testimony. People stood and told what God had done in their lives that year, that week. A healing, a rescue, a long night, a turning point. Bread for the body, and a story for everyone else to chew on. Methodists keep it distinct from the Lord's Supper. It isn't communion; it's fellowship. Other churches keep their own forms. Moravians hold a lovefeast with sweet buns and coffee, served while the congregation sings. The Church of the Brethren keeps a love feast with footwashing, a full meal and then communion, following Jesus at the Last Supper. Different tables, the same old word. And this week has been full of rooms like this. Gelassenheit, letting go. A village that forgave. The silence of a Quaker meeting, and the queries carried into it. How is it with your soul? A covenant renewed. And now bread and a story. Anabaptists, Quakers, Methodists: three rooms where ordinary people carry a great deal of the faith together, around a plain table.

Here's the practice: remember a table that fed you more than food. Let your breath settle. Bring to mind one meal: a kitchen, a hospital tray, a picnic, a stranger's dinner. Who was there? What story got told? Stay with it a moment. If you pray, you can give thanks for it. If you don't, simply thank the people who were there, wherever they are now. Then think of one person you could break bread with this week, and the true story you'd bring. The bell holds the time.
The love feast. A plain shared meal, bread and water, with stories of what God has done, kept by Methodists, Moravians, Brethren and others.
Your line: bread and a story. Today, share something simple to eat with someone, and tell them one true thing that happened to you. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-nine.

howItsDone: At a Methodist love feast, plain bread and water are shared and people tell what God has done in their lives; Moravians hold a lovefeast with buns and coffee during singing, and the Church of the Brethren keeps a love feast with footwashing, a meal and communion.

fork.setup: you're in Corinth, and the shared meal has split into rich and poor eating apart. what does Paul do?
options: let it go; it's only dinner.
rebuke them: one is hungry, another drunken.
cancel the shared meal for good.
fork.reveal: he rebukes them sharply. the early church kept eating together anyway, and the love feast is that table, kept plain.

original.note: Greek: love. in Jude 12 its plural names the love feasts, which the King James calls feasts of charity.

trapdoor: what you thought: a big church potluck.
what it means: a plain shared meal, bread and water, where the stories are the main course.
what a scholar hears: Jude 12's "feasts of charity" renders the Greek agapais, love feasts; 1 Corinthians 11 shows an early shared meal going wrong.
recall: leaving home for the love of God

Wesley learning the love feast from the Moravians is stated as fact; confirm. Methodist form (plain bread or cake, water, a shared cup, testimonies) and its distinction from the Lord's Supper are general; confirm.
Moravian lovefeast (sweet buns and coffee during singing) and Church of the Brethren love feast (footwashing, meal, communion) are described as practice; confirm.
Acts 2:46 quoted in two pieces in the voice, both exact KJV; 'meat there just means food' is a gloss on KJV usage.
